credit_metrics.text: EBITDA increased by {{ebitda.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda@FY2025}}, lifting operating profit by {{operating_profit.change@FY2025}} to {{operating_profit@FY2025}}.
Total debt rose by {{total_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{total_debt@FY2025}}, so gross leverage was broadly unchanged at {{gross_leverage@FY2025}}.
Interest coverage improved to {{interest_coverage@FY2025}}, up {{interest_coverage.change@FY2025}} on the prior year.
FFO rose by {{ffo.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo@FY2025}}, leaving FFO to debt stable at {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}}.

Free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}} as capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}, taking FCF to debt down to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}}.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_like@FY2025}}, and cash liquidity declined by the same amount to {{cash_liquidity@FY2025}}.

Advance ticket cover rose by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2025}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}}, with contract liabilities up {{contract_liabilities.change@FY2025}} to {{contract_liabilities@FY2025}}.
The company redeemed its New Capital Perpetual Bonds in full during the year, removing that instrument from the capital structure.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2025}} to {{passengers@FY2025}}, supported by a summer programme of new leisure routes.
Fuel made up {{fuel_share_of_costs@FY2025}} of costs, broadly unchanged on the prior year and in line with the peer median.
The company acquired previously leased Boeing 737-800 aircraft and exercised its option for additional 737 MAX 8 aircraft, which it says supports recurring cost savings.

peer_positioning.text: Norwegian sits in the middle of the low-cost group on EBITDA margin ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@2025}}), net leverage ({{net_leverage.peer_rank@2025}}) and gross leverage ({{gross_leverage.peer_rank@2025}}).

Interest coverage, FFO to debt and FCF to debt also rank {{interest_coverage.peer_rank@2025}}, {{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@2025}} and {{fcf_to_debt.peer_rank@2025}} respectively, each in line with the group median.

Capex intensity of {{capex_intensity@FY2025}} is above the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@2025}}, while cash liquidity to revenue of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}} is below the median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@2025}}.
Advance ticket cover of {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}} is the lowest of the group ({{advance_ticket_cover.peer_rank@2025}}), below the peer median of {{advance_ticket_cover.peer_median@2025}}.

snapshot.text: Norwegian Air Shuttle, the low-cost carrier, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{revenue@FY2025}} in FY2025 while paying an initial dividend to shareholders.

Net leverage rose by {{net_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{net_leverage@FY2025}} as net debt increased by {{net_debt.change@FY2025}}, although the EBITDA margin widened by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}}.

Liquidity is the point to watch: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}, the weakest of the low-cost peers ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@2025}}).

watch_items.text: Leverage: net leverage rose by {{net_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{net_leverage@FY2025}} as net debt grew by {{net_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{net_debt@FY2025}}, so debt reduction is the key sensitivity.

Cash generation: FCF to debt fell by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}} as capex intensity of {{capex_intensity@FY2025}} sits above the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@2025}}.

Liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}} is the weakest of the group ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@2025}}), below the peer median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@2025}}.

Customer prepayments: advance ticket cover of {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}} is below the peer median of {{advance_ticket_cover.peer_median@2025}}, so a smaller share of the cash buffer comes from forward bookings.
